examples.solution_text:
(a) All four vertices point outwards. Every interior angle is less than $180^{\circ}$, so it is convex.
(b) The outline turns inwards at $C$. The interior angle at $C$ is reflex, so it is non-convex.

examples.question_text:
Decide whether each quadrilateral is convex or non-convex. Give a reason.
(a) Its interior angles are $135^{\circ}$, $85^{\circ}$, $75^{\circ}$ and $65^{\circ}$.
(b) Its interior angles are $225^{\circ}$, $55^{\circ}$, $45^{\circ}$ and $35^{\circ}$.
(c) It is a rectangle.
examples.solution_text:
(a) Every angle is less than $180^{\circ}$, so it is convex.
(b) $225^{\circ}$ is reflex. One reflex interior angle makes it non-convex.
(c) All four angles of a rectangle are $90^{\circ}$. None is reflex, so it is convex.

(a) Both diagonals lie inside the outline and cross inside it. The quadrilateral is convex.
(b) Diagonal $BD$ lies outside the outline. The quadrilateral is non-convex.
(c) One diagonal inside is not enough. Both must lie inside for a convex quadrilateral. $BD$ lies outside, and the interior angle at $C$ is reflex.

methods.description: Classify a quadrilateral from its outline: identify an inward turn and its reflex interior angle, or establish that every interior angle is less than 180 degrees. Thinness and rotation do not change this test.

methods.description: Classify using both diagonal segments: both lie within a convex quadrilateral and intersect inside it; a non-convex quadrilateral has an exterior diagonal. One interior diagonal alone is insufficient.

methods.description: Apply the interior-angle definition to supplied angle measures or known right angles: all angles below 180 degrees imply convexity; a reflex interior angle implies non-convexity. Retained supplementary coverage.
